plan.contextChunk: This figure plots the probability simplex for a three-class problem on a set of three-dimensional coordinate axes. The axes are black arrows radiating from a shared origin: y_1 runs to the right, y_2 runs straight up, and y_3 runs down and to the left toward the viewer. Each axis carries a single tick labeled 1, and each unit point is annotated with a bold class name, Car at y_1 equal to 1, Bike at y_2 equal to 1, and Bird at y_3 equal to 1. A translucent pink triangle is filled in with its three corners resting exactly on those unit points, and the stretches of axis inside the triangle are drawn darker where the shading passes over them. The slanted face, not the volume it cuts off, is what carries the meaning: only points on that plane are admissible, the geometric form of requiring three nonnegative scores that sum to one. The drawing accompanies the definition of a classifier as a mapping from RGB images into the (K-1)-dimensional simplex, here with K equal to 3, where each vertex is an unambiguous prediction of one class and interior points are graded mixtures.

elements: Origin at (0,0,0) where the three axes meet
Black axis arrow y1 running to screen-right, past the unit point, with a solid arrowhead
Black axis arrow y2 running straight up, past the unit point, with a solid arrowhead
Black axis arrow y3 running down-and-left toward the viewer, past the unit point, with a solid arrowhead
Italic axis labels 'y1' (right of the y1 arrowhead), 'y2' (above the y2 arrowhead), 'y3' (below-left of the y3 arrowhead)
Tick label '1' at each unit point: left of (1,0,0), left of (0,1,0), above-left of (0,0,1)
Bold class labels: 'Car' below-right of the y1 unit point, 'Bike' right of the y2 unit point, 'Bird' below-right of the y3 unit point
Translucent pink filled triangle with corners exactly at (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1)
Dark red segments of each axis from the origin out to its unit point (the portions the triangle shades over)
Draggable probability point marker constrained to the triangle interior
Three thin guide lines / dropped coordinates from the draggable point to the three axes (shown while dragging)
Numeric readout panel showing y1, y2, y3 and their sum = 1

interactions.teaches: The pink triangle is a flat slanted plane slicing the positive octant, not a solid body — rotating until it is seen edge-on shows that all admissible score vectors lie on a single 2D surface in 3D space.

Moving the point anywhere on the triangle changes the three class confidences continuously, but y1 + y2 + y3 always stays exactly 1 — the simplex is the geometric form of the nonnegativity-plus-sum-to-one constraint, so confidence can only be traded between classes, never created.

Clicking Car, Bike, or Bird snaps the point to that corner, driving the other two coordinates to 0 — a vertex is a one-hot, unambiguous prediction, while everything strictly inside is a graded mixture of classes.
Viewing the same point in the ambient 3D axes versus flat-on the triangle shows that a 3-class distribution really has only K-1 = 2 degrees of freedom.
interactions.label: View

demo_steps.title: The constraint plane
demo_steps.narration: Three axes y1, y2, y3 carry the scores for Car, Bike and Bird. The pink triangle joins the three unit points: every point on it has nonnegative coordinates summing to 1.

demo_steps.title: Mixtures inside
demo_steps.narration: Drag the marker around the interior. The readouts shift — more Car means less Bike and Bird — but the sum is pinned at 1, so confidence is only ever redistributed.

demo_steps.title: Vertices are certain answers
demo_steps.narration: Click 'Car'. The point snaps to (1,0,0) and the other two coordinates collapse to zero: a corner of the simplex is an unambiguous single-class prediction.

demo_steps.title: Only two degrees of freedom
demo_steps.narration: Looking straight down onto the plane, the simplex is just a flat triangle: for K = 3 classes the output lives in a (K-1) = 2-dimensional set.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: 1 probability unit = 1 world unit. Map y1 -> +X (screen-right), y2 -> +Y (screen-up), y3 -> +Z (receding diagonal that projects down-and-left toward the viewer under the standard isometric pose; if the default pose sends +Z up-right, negate it so the Bird axis reads down-left as in the source). Axis shafts run from the origin out to 1.45 units with cone arrowheads ~0.09 long, 0.045 radius, line width ~4px; scene spans roughly -0.2..1.6 on each axis. Triangle vertices exactly (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1), rendered double-sided, flat-shaded, no lighting. Colors: axes beyond the unit points pure black #000000; the origin-to-unit-point stretch of each axis dark maroon #5A0F0F (it reads darker because the pink fill passes over it); triangle fill #F7B3B3 at ~0.75 opacity (source is a light salmon pink, no stroke on the triangle edges other than where they coincide with the axes); draggable marker a solid dark red #B11226 sphere of radius ~0.045; guide lines thin dashed #B11226 at 0.5 opacity. Labels are black, rendered as screen-facing sprites: italic serif 'y1' right of the +X arrowhead, 'y2' just above the +Y arrowhead, 'y3' below-left of the y3 arrowhead; serif '1' tick numerals placed just inside/left of each unit point; bold sans class names 'Car' below-right of (1,0,0), 'Bike' immediately right of (0,1,0), 'Bird' below-right of (0,0,1). Point constraint math: barycentric coords (y1,y2,y3) with yi >= 0 and y1+y2+y3 = 1; project any dragged 3D position onto the plane x+y+z=1 then clamp into the triangle. Default point position is the centroid (1/3, 1/3, 1/3).
interactionPlan.notes: Build with an orthographic camera to preserve the flat axonometric look; the isometric pose keeps the three axes roughly 120 degrees apart on screen as in the source. Triangle: BufferGeometry with the three vertices, MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xF7B3B3, transparent: true, opacity: 0.75, side: DoubleSide, depthWrite: false }) so the dark axis segments show through cleanly. Draw the maroon inner axis segments as separate Line objects from the black outer segments rather than recoloring one line. Dragging: raycast onto an invisible plane mesh coplanar with the triangle, then clamp barycentric coordinates to >= 0 and renormalize so the sum stays exactly 1; update a DOM readout (y1, y2, y3, sum). Vertex clicks: raycast against small invisible pick spheres at the three unit points plus their label sprites; tween the marker to the corner over ~350 ms. 'Flat-on simplex' toggle tweens the camera to look down the (1,1,1) direction and fades out the parts of the axes outside the triangle. Labels via CSS2DRenderer or canvas sprites with constant screen size so text stays legible during orbit.

where $0>\hat{y}_c>1$. In the toy example with three classes shown
previously, the valid solutions for
$\hat{\mathbf{y}}=[\hat{y}_1, \hat{y}_2, \hat{y}_3]^\mathsf{T}$ are

Simplex with three exclusive classes:

Under this formulation, the function $f$ is a mapping
$f:\mathbb{R}^{N \times M \times 3} \rightarrow \vartriangle^{K-1}$ from
the set of red-green-blue (RGB) images to the $(K-1)$-dimensional
simplex, $\vartriangle^{K-1}$.

discrepancies: The y₃ axis is much more foreshortened than in the source, where it extends far to the lower-left; combined with a slightly higher camera elevation this makes the generated triangle look narrower/smaller than the wide pink triangle of the original.

Added elements not in the source: a dark-red draggable marker sphere, three dashed red guide lines and foot dots inside the triangle (pedagogically motivated, but they change the clean look of the original).
The inner (0→1) axis segments read as washed-out brown/pink through the semi-transparent triangle rather than the strong dark maroon of the source.

Class-name labels ('Car', 'Bike', 'Bird') are noticeably smaller and less dominant than the heavy bold labels in the source; 'Car' sits to the left of its vertex whereas the source places it just below/right of the unit point.
Arrowheads are smaller/stubbier relative to axis length than the prominent triangular arrowheads in the source.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and well-built 3D rendition of the probability-simplex figure with correct axes, triangle, colors and labels plus rich, conceptually meaningful interactions (drag marker, vertex snaps, flat-on view, guided demo); main shortcomings are the over-foreshortened y₃ axis that shrinks the triangle relative to the source and slightly understated maroon axes / class labels.
action_items: Adjust the default camera (increase the y₃ screen angle / lower elevation) so the y₃ axis projects further down-left and the pink triangle spans a similar area to the source.
Render the inner 0→1 axis segments after/over the triangle (or raise their renderOrder / use depthTest ordering) so they read as solid dark maroon as in the source.
Increase the bold class-label font size and reposition 'Car' to the lower-right of its vertex to match the source's label hierarchy and placement.
Enlarge the axis arrowheads slightly so they match the prominent arrow tips of the original diagram.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (no failure modes, no plan action items); remaining issues are implementation details like camera angle, render order, label sizing, and arrowhead scale.

plan.contextChunk: This figure plots the probability simplex for a three-class problem on a set of three-dimensional coordinate axes. The axes are black arrows radiating from a shared origin: y_1 runs to the right, y_2 runs straight up, and y_3 runs down and to the left toward the viewer. Each axis carries a single tick labeled 1, and each unit point is annotated with a bold class name, Car at y_1 equal to 1, Bike at y_2 equal to 1, and Bird at y_3 equal to 1. A translucent pink triangle is filled in with its three corners resting exactly on those unit points, and the stretches of axis inside the triangle are drawn darker where the shading passes over them. The slanted face, not the volume it cuts off, is what carries the meaning: only points on that plane are admissible, the geometric form of requiring three nonnegative scores that sum to one. The drawing accompanies the definition of a classifier as a mapping from RGB images into the (K-1)-dimensional simplex, here with K equal to 3, where each vertex is an unambiguous prediction of one class and interior points are graded mixtures.

elements: Origin at (0,0,0) where the three axes meet
Black axis arrow y1 running to screen-right, past the unit point, with a solid arrowhead
Black axis arrow y2 running straight up, past the unit point, with a solid arrowhead
Black axis arrow y3 running down-and-left toward the viewer, past the unit point, with a solid arrowhead
Italic axis labels 'y1' (right of the y1 arrowhead), 'y2' (above the y2 arrowhead), 'y3' (below-left of the y3 arrowhead)
Tick label '1' at each unit point: left of (1,0,0), left of (0,1,0), above-left of (0,0,1)
Bold class labels: 'Car' below-right of the y1 unit point, 'Bike' right of the y2 unit point, 'Bird' below-right of the y3 unit point
Translucent pink filled triangle with corners exactly at (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1)
Dark red segments of each axis from the origin out to its unit point (the portions the triangle shades over)
Draggable probability point marker constrained to the triangle interior
Three thin guide lines / dropped coordinates from the draggable point to the three axes (shown while dragging)
Numeric readout panel showing y1, y2, y3 and their sum = 1

interactions.teaches: The pink triangle is a flat slanted plane slicing the positive octant, not a solid body — rotating until it is seen edge-on shows that all admissible score vectors lie on a single 2D surface in 3D space.

Moving the point anywhere on the triangle changes the three class confidences continuously, but y1 + y2 + y3 always stays exactly 1 — the simplex is the geometric form of the nonnegativity-plus-sum-to-one constraint, so confidence can only be traded between classes, never created.

Clicking Car, Bike, or Bird snaps the point to that corner, driving the other two coordinates to 0 — a vertex is a one-hot, unambiguous prediction, while everything strictly inside is a graded mixture of classes.
Viewing the same point in the ambient 3D axes versus flat-on the triangle shows that a 3-class distribution really has only K-1 = 2 degrees of freedom.

demo_steps.title: The constraint plane
demo_steps.narration: Three axes y1, y2, y3 carry the scores for Car, Bike and Bird. The pink triangle joins the three unit points: every point on it has nonnegative coordinates summing to 1.

demo_steps.title: Mixtures inside
demo_steps.narration: Drag the marker around the interior. The readouts shift — more Car means less Bike and Bird — but the sum is pinned at 1, so confidence is only ever redistributed.

demo_steps.title: Vertices are certain answers
demo_steps.narration: Click 'Car'. The point snaps to (1,0,0) and the other two coordinates collapse to zero: a corner of the simplex is an unambiguous single-class prediction.

demo_steps.title: Only two degrees of freedom
demo_steps.narration: Looking straight down onto the plane, the simplex is just a flat triangle: for K = 3 classes the output lives in a (K-1) = 2-dimensional set.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: 1 probability unit = 1 world unit. Map y1 -> +X (screen-right), y2 -> +Y (screen-up), y3 -> +Z (receding diagonal that projects down-and-left toward the viewer under the standard isometric pose; if the default pose sends +Z up-right, negate it so the Bird axis reads down-left as in the source). Axis shafts run from the origin out to 1.45 units with cone arrowheads ~0.09 long, 0.045 radius, line width ~4px; scene spans roughly -0.2..1.6 on each axis. Triangle vertices exactly (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1), rendered double-sided, flat-shaded, no lighting. Colors: axes beyond the unit points pure black #000000; the origin-to-unit-point stretch of each axis dark maroon #5A0F0F (it reads darker because the pink fill passes over it); triangle fill #F7B3B3 at ~0.75 opacity (source is a light salmon pink, no stroke on the triangle edges other than where they coincide with the axes); draggable marker a solid dark red #B11226 sphere of radius ~0.045; guide lines thin dashed #B11226 at 0.5 opacity. Labels are black, rendered as screen-facing sprites: italic serif 'y1' right of the +X arrowhead, 'y2' just above the +Y arrowhead, 'y3' below-left of the y3 arrowhead; serif '1' tick numerals placed just inside/left of each unit point; bold sans class names 'Car' below-right of (1,0,0), 'Bike' immediately right of (0,1,0), 'Bird' below-right of (0,0,1). Point constraint math: barycentric coords (y1,y2,y3) with yi >= 0 and y1+y2+y3 = 1; project any dragged 3D position onto the plane x+y+z=1 then clamp into the triangle. Default point position is the centroid (1/3, 1/3, 1/3).
interactionPlan.notes: Build with an orthographic camera to preserve the flat axonometric look; the isometric pose keeps the three axes roughly 120 degrees apart on screen as in the source. Triangle: BufferGeometry with the three vertices, MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xF7B3B3, transparent: true, opacity: 0.75, side: DoubleSide, depthWrite: false }) so the dark axis segments show through cleanly. Draw the maroon inner axis segments as separate Line objects from the black outer segments rather than recoloring one line. Dragging: raycast onto an invisible plane mesh coplanar with the triangle, then clamp barycentric coordinates to >= 0 and renormalize so the sum stays exactly 1; update a DOM readout (y1, y2, y3, sum). Vertex clicks: raycast against small invisible pick spheres at the three unit points plus their label sprites; tween the marker to the corner over ~350 ms. 'Flat-on simplex' toggle tweens the camera to look down the (1,1,1) direction and fades out the parts of the axes outside the triangle. Labels via CSS2DRenderer or canvas sprites with constant screen size so text stays legible during orbit.
